<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par122 />''fire'' (rarely {{GHGterm|masc.}}); {{GHGheb|text=נֹ֫גַהּ|translate=brightness}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫בֶן|translate=a stone}}, as a rule also {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ|translate=wind, spirit}}; {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=breath, soul}}; also {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר|translate=light}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=36|verse=32}}, and others.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|p}}
'''4.''' The following classes of ideas, which are also regarded as feminine in Hebrew (see above, ''h''), are usually indicated by the feminine ''form'', notwithstanding their occasional transference to masculine persons (see ''r'' and ''s''):

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|q}}
(''a'') Abstracts<ref>Cf. the list of masculine and feminine abstracts in Albrecht, l. c., 1896, p. 111 ff.</ref> (sometimes along with masculine forms from the same stem, as {{GHGheb|text=נְקָמָה|translate=vengeance}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=נָקָם}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶזְרָה|translate=help}}, as well as {{GHGheb|text=עֵ֫זֶר}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֱמוּנָה|translate=firmness, faithfulness}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּבוּרָה|translate=strength}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּדוּלָה|translate=greatness}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלֵאָה|translate=fullness}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֶמְשָׁלָה|translate=dominion}}, &c. Similarly, the feminine (sing. and plur.) of adjectives and participles is used substantivally in the sense of the Latin and Greek ''neuter'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=נְכוֹנָה|translate=stedfastness}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=טוֹבָה|translate=goodness}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָעָה|translate=evil}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=50|verse=20}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְקַלָּה|translate=a light thing}} (i.e. a trifling thing), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=14}}; so especially in the plural, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֹלוֹת|translate=great things}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַנֶּֽהֱרָסוֹת|translate=the ruined places}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=36}}, along with {{GHGheb|text=הַנְּשַׁמָּה|translate=that which was desolate}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֹבוֹת|translate=kindnesses}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=28}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְכֹחוֹת|translate=uprightness, honesty}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְעִימוֹת|translate=amoena}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=11}} (but in verse 6 in the same sense {{GHGheb|text=נְעִימִים}}), {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָאוֹת|translate=wonderful things}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=10}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=קָשׁוֹת|translate=hard things, roughly}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=7}}, 30 (but cf. also {{GHGheb|text=רֵיקִים|translate=vain things}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=12|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=28|verse=19|hidebook=1}}). Cf. moreover, the very frequent use of {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} (as well as {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}} and {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=23}}, &c., in the sense of ''hoc, illud'' (also {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה}} equivalent to ''illa'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=19}}): also the use of the feminine form of the verb in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא תָקוּם וְלֹא תִֽהְיֶה|translate=it shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=7}}; so too the suffixes {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=18}}, referring back to a whole statement.<ref>While in all these instances it is simplest to speak of the ''feminine'' in Hebrew as being used ''for the neuter'' (which in Latin, Greek, and German is commonly employed for similar purposes), it must yet not be forgotten that since the language is wholly wanting in ''neuters'', the Semitic mind regarded the above-mentioned forms primarily as actual feminines. Hence the Arab commentators are accustomed to explain the feminines of adjectives and participles (which would be neuter in Latin, &c.) by supplying a feminine substantive.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|r}}
(''b'') Titles and designations of office, properly a subdivision of the abstract ideas treated above, under ''q'', and specially noticed here only on account of their peculiar transference to concrete male persons. Thus we have {{GHGheb|text=קֹהֶ֫לֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=1}}, &c. (as a title of Solomon), properly no doubt ''that which takes part in'' or ''speaks in a religious assembly'', hence LXX ἐκκλησιαστής, i.e. ''concionator, preacher''; the proper names {{GHGheb|text=סֹפֶ֫רֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=2|verse=55}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=57}}, and {{GHGheb|text=פֹּכֶ֫רֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=2|verse=57}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=7|verse=59}}, and the foreign word {{GHGheb|text=פֶּחָה|translate=viceroy}}; in the plural {{GHGheb|text=כְּנָוֹת}} prop. ''cognomina'', then ''like-named, colleagues''; {{GHGheb|text=פְּרָעוֹת|translate=princes}} (if this be the true meaning).<ref>This use of the feminine form is far more frequent in Arabic, Ethiopic, and Aramaic; cf. e.g. in Arabic ''ḥalîfa'' (fem. from ''ḥalîf'', following after, taking the place of) in the sense of ''the'' successor or representative (of Muḥammad), and ''ʿallāma'' (''great wisdom'') as a title of learned men. Analogous to this is the Latin ''magistratus, magistracy'', for ''magistrate'', and our ''his Majesty, Excellency, Highness'', &c.</ref> All these words, in accordance with their meaning, are construed as masculine (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=7|verse=27}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=אָֽמְרָה ק׳}} the words should rather be divided as {{GHGheb|text=אָמַר הַקּ׳}}; cf. 12:8).
